paper.title: Computation of the incomplete gamma function for negative values of the argument (Algorithm 969)

code.note: Fortran 90 module IncgamNEG (incgamNEG.f90), with setprecision, cons, gammaError. Driver testgamstar.f90 and its shipped output OutGammStar are in Fortran90/Drivers. Compile with gfortran; the constants file is in Src.

claim.location: Shipped driver Fortran90/Drivers/testgamstar.f90: DATA igams entry 11 (0.98117651308252274), which is gamma*(a,z) at a=-0.03, z=-0.03. The same value is printed in the shipped OutGammStar file on the row '-.3000D-01 -.3000D-01 0.9811765130825D+00'. Paper location for the accuracy claim: arXiv:1608.04152 abstract, relative accuracy about 1e-13 in [-500,500] x [-500,0).
claim.metric: gamma*(a,z) = z**(-a) gamma(a,z)/Gamma(a) at a=-0.03, z=-0.03, as printed by incgamstar in the shipped driver
claim.paper_value: 0.98117651308252274 (shipped expected value; the paper prints no table of this value)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The paper states relative accuracy about 1e-13 in this region; the shipped driver prints 13 significant digits. 1e-9 absolute (about 1e-9 relative at this value) is about 1e4 times the stated accuracy: loose enough for compiler and precision differences, tight enough to reject a wrong branch, since other branches differ by orders of magnitude.

cost.data_size: None; the value is in the driver's DATA statements.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence of the archive; the rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The gamma* function has no closed form at a=-0.03, and the shipped driver compares the computed value with precomputed reference values, so a rebuild must run the series or asymptotic method.
